results.grokRaw:
The youth's palms had not yet regained color when the first elder spoke my name aloud. The mated-pair trees pressed their leaf-curtains closer, as though the grove itself sought to contain what had already escaped. Accusations rose like heat from the spiralgrass: that the wish had been meant for spectacle, not truth, that the Sacrificiant had known and remained silent on purpose. I felt the weight of every gaze settle on the place where my lineage should have stayed hidden. My alignment sense caught the fracture in the youth's intent the moment it formed, yet the gossamer band across my mouth turned every warning into a muffled sound no one heeded.

The sigil on my wrist flared without warning. A single brilliant flame licked upward, consuming the pale mark that had never shown itself in public before. The elders fell silent. One stepped back, hand raised as if warding off the light itself. I tried to shape an explanation with my eyes alone, the only language left to me, but the flame kept rising, steady and accusing, revealing the bloodline I had carried in secret since childhood. The youth stared at her own cold palms, then at me, as if the two sights belonged to the same broken rite.

Julian's stormy blue eyes would have deepened the way they always did when he weighed a hidden cost. He would have watched the flame the way he watched every alignment that refused to lie, and he would have measured whether I still chose silence. The memory pressed against the present until I could almost feel the ring he turned on his finger, the small silver scar at his brow catching the light the same way the sigil now did.

I raised my unbound hand, palm outward, the only gesture I could offer that might still the rising voices. The elders waited. The youth's bare foot slid another inch across the grass, as if she might flee the chamber before anyone demanded more from either of us. The flame on my wrist burned lower but did not vanish, leaving a faint after-image that every eye present now carried.

I realize that old tarot deck is still in my hand. Reassuringly solid. Present. One of the heavy gold cards slips out — "Petition Fate" is inscribed in it. If only it were that easy. I would wish myself a way out. No — a way in. If only…
